title: How Coinbase earns — and where the dollars actually pool
thesis: Two demand pools (trading fees + interest on USDC/cash) fan into Coinbase's product lines, then pool back onto the partners that catch the economics: Circle (USDC issuer), the banks holding reserves, and the L1 networks Coinbase stakes into.

cards.title: Transaction fees
cards.body: *$4.06B* of FY2025 transaction revenue — *$3.32B* of it from consumers paying a spread — swings with crypto prices and volume; *BTC + ETH* alone drove *~45%* of Trading Volume.

cards.title: USDC reserve interest
cards.body: Stablecoin revenue hit *$1.35B* (+48% YoY). Under the *Circle Agreement*, Coinbase keeps *100%* of interest on USDC held in its own products and shares Circle's off-platform reserve economics — one counterparty (*Circle*) was *19%* of total revenue.

cards.title: Circle issues USDC
cards.body: Circle is the *issuer* of USDC and holds the trademarks; Coinbase distributes it. The economics depend on the USDC market cap (part of a *~$300B+* stablecoin market) and short-term interest rates.

cards.title: Blockchain rewards
cards.body: Coinbase staked *~$7.5B* of consumer assets into ETH/SOL-type networks, earning *$0.68B* of blockchain rewards — it keeps a commission and passes the rest to customers.

cards.title: Deribit + futures
cards.body: The *$4.3B* Deribit acquisition (closed Aug 2025) bolted on the world's largest crypto-options venue, pushing Coinbase into international and US derivatives — Q4 derivatives revenue hit an all-time high.

cards.title: Rates do the lifting
cards.body: Both the *$1.35B* stablecoin line and *$0.25B* interest income ride on short-term rates; Coinbase guided Q1'26 S&S to *$550–$630M* citing *lower effective interest rates* — the single biggest swing variable below trading.

source: COIN FY2025 10-K (Note 4 Revenue; Circle Agreement; staking disclosure) + Q4'25 shareholder letter, 2026-02-12
